correctness.rationale: Exact block exponential and shear singular values yield the whole minimum-modulus trichotomy, including a unique rescaled saddle and critical stationary point; compact block decomposition yields all spectral sets. For positive expansiveness, Huynh Theorem 5.1 is applied only after checking its three hypotheses. For negative expansiveness the explicit normalized near-cancellation vectors, periodic-time shift and increasing reparametrizations give a uniform discrepancy tending to zero while requiring a forbidden orbit delay. The 130 finite checker assertions supplement, not replace, these infinite-dimensional proofs.

originality.rationale: The motivating theorem covers the uniformly lower-bounded positive branch, but its diagonal classification does not imply the sharp nilpotent-coupling phase boundary or the explicit negative Bowen–Walters witness. Spectral sets are identical across couplings despite opposite dynamics. An earlier foundational paper supplies necessary spectral restrictions only in its accessible abstract. Specific older-full-text risk remains; novelty is qualified rather than inferred from search silence.
residual_risks: The Lee–Morales full text could contain an unindexed triangular example or equivalent spectral-indistinguishability argument; the abstract does not resolve this.
Older literature on continuous-time nonnormal semigroup shadowing might contain a theorem implying the same exact exponent threshold without terminology overlap.
The scope is fixed two-dimensional Jordan blocks with power-law scales, not arbitrary compact perturbations or Banach-space norm geometries.

value.rationale: The theorem gives two bounded, generator-bounded-below, pointwise escaping uniformly continuous semigroups with identical generator and all-time spectral sets but opposite Bowen–Walters positive expansiveness. The exact sharp coupling boundary identifies when nonnormal transient cancellation defeats reparametrized orbit separation, and the polynomial singular-collapse constant, critical plateau and eventual lower-modulus restoration quantify that mechanism.
